A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AtSpeed research. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and matching algorithms, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison despite substantial appendix expansion.

before.justification: V1 reports original acceleration and recommendation experiments on Amazon Beauty and Games, including component ablations, parameter studies, and training-resource measurements.

after.justification: V3 retains original Beauty and Games experiments and adds MovieLens-1M and Goodreads evaluations, further ranking results, and extended parameter analysis.

M1.justification: The AtSpeed-S and AtSpeed-R losses, drafting procedures, verification algorithms, and tree-based attention remain substantively unchanged. V3's corrected acceptance condition, explicit recommendation-loss formula, and attention implementation explanation revise mathematics or documentation rather than establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates recommendation on Amazon Beauty and Games. V3 additionally evaluates MovieLens-1M and Goodreads, extending the represented domains to movies and books (Appendix A.3.2, Table 6). These are actual benchmark evaluations, not merely cited datasets.

E2.justification: V3 adds retrieval-based DARE to the acceleration comparisons; v1 only discusses DARE in related work. Recommendation-accuracy comparisons also expand from AtSpeed-R versus the target LLM in v1 Table 2 to include SFT, WordKD, TVDKD, SeqKD, DARE, and both AtSpeed variants in v3 Table 5. Together these substantially broaden the evaluated comparisons.

E3.justification: V3 adds NDCG to the evaluation metrics and extends the AtSpeed-R alignment-strength sweep to 0.9 and 1.0. The temperature-0.5 evaluation reported in v1 Table 2 is absent. The original Beauty/Games splits, model sizes, training budget, and default decoding settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 3 adds Recall@10 measurements to the existing component ablations, and Figure 5 extends the alignment-strength sensitivity analysis to extreme values. The earlier temperature-0.5 accuracy/speed comparison is removed. Tree-attention analysis, draft-length sensitivity, additional-training-data analysis, and the timing case study are retained, sometimes relocated.

E5.justification: Neither PDF reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for the experiments. V3's new averages aggregate across recommendation-list sizes or methods; they do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: V3 adds extensive DARE, ranking-quality, movie/book, and alignment-strength results. Among matched Beauty entries, strict AtSpeed-S WS@20 changes from 1.82 to 1.84, and relaxed AtSpeed-R AS@10 changes from 2.10 to 2.01 (v1 Table 1; v3 Tables 1 and 4). Temperature-0.5 results disappear. These are reported result changes, without evidence that the retained experiments were rerun.

T1.justification: V3 corrects strict acceptance from a condition on every drafted sequence to existence of a qualifying K-element subset. Appendix A.2 replaces the short sampling-limit argument with a log-Stirling/Taylor derivation and explicit approximation term, changes the population interpretation from vocabulary to sequences, and develops context marginalization and an acceptance-rate proof. These substantially revise mathematical reasoning, although the intended conclusions remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: N-to-K speculative decoding for recommendation, two alignment objectives, relaxed verification, and approximately twofold acceleration. Additional supporting experiments do not materially redefine these claims.

C2.justification: V3 adds substantive qualifications about relaxed verification: weaker NDCG is attributed to alignment without explicit ordering, and poorer large-K speedup on smaller catalogs is tentatively linked to concentrated draft probabilities. It also adds explanations for DARE's performance and differing sensitivity to alignment strength. These expand the discussion of mechanisms and applicability beyond v1's primarily favorable speed/Recall interpretation.

D1.justification: V3 supplies an explicit repository address where v1's abstract promises a future release and its reproducibility statement mentions anonymous code. Appendix A.3.1 newly specifies the existing recommendation loss and explains sequence flattening and attention-mask construction with an example. Added datasets receive statistics and source references; existing training hyperparameters and hardware disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V3 adds an explicit distinction from SpecGR's cold-start item speculation and several references on LLM and traditional recommendation. It removes two previously cited Li papers and replaces the Stirling-approximation reference. The principal positioning around N-to-K verification, DistillSpec, and DARE remains intact.

P1.justification: The appendix's theoretical exposition is extensively rewritten into three structured derivation subsections, and experimental settings are separated from additional results. Recommendation accuracy is integrated into overall performance, reducing four research questions to three. These substantial explanatory and organizational revisions accompany smaller wording and author-affiliation edits.

P2.justification: Table 1 is redesigned around selected list sizes, averages, and accuracy columns, with full acceleration results presented in appendix Table 4. V3 adds a beam-sequence example and movie/book results table, expands dataset statistics, and replaces the temperature table with broader accuracy displays. Figure 3 gains accuracy annotations, Figure 5 extends its axes, and several retained figures and tables move.

improvement.justification: V3 strengthens empirical scrutiny through broader domain comparisons and ranking metrics that expose accuracy and speed tradeoffs, while its repository address and attention implementation improve reproducibility. These gains are tempered by removal of the temperature-0.5 comparison, inconsistent new results—DARE's Beauty relaxed WS@20 is 1.69 in Table 1 but 1.95 in Table 4—and errors in the revised theoretical support, including omitted q(y) weighting in the new Theorem 2 proof. The net improvement is useful but limited.
